title: Symphony No. 7 in A major
hook: Four movements, each driven by a single rhythm; Wagner called it the apotheosis of the dance.

painting.title: The Peasant Dance
painting.pairingNote: Villagers stamp and spin to the drone of a bagpipe; Wagner called the Seventh “the apotheosis of the dance”, and its trio has a drone of its own.

facts: Beethoven wrote the Seventh in 1811–12, partly while taking the cure at the Bohemian spa town of Teplitz. It is dedicated to Count Moritz von Fries.

It was first performed on 8 December 1813 in Vienna, with Beethoven conducting, at a charity concert for soldiers wounded at the Battle of Hanau, weeks after Napoleon’s defeat at Leipzig. The same concert introduced his patriotic *Wellington’s Victory*. The orchestra included the violinist Louis Spohr and the composers Hummel, Meyerbeer and Salieri.
The audience demanded the second movement again on the spot. Beethoven himself called the symphony one of his best works.
Each movement is driven by one rhythm, repeated with tremendous energy. Richard Wagner called the Seventh “the apotheosis of the dance”.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a slow awakening and a leaping dance (I), a solemn procession (II), a whirlwind with a hymn at its heart (III), a wild, stamping finale (IV).

movements.heading: Poco sostenuto – Vivace
movements.summary: A long, slow introduction climbs through vast scales and visits two distant keys. Then a single note is tapped back and forth until it turns into a dance. From there the movement never lets go of one skipping rhythm: long, short, long.

mainIdeas.name: The scales
mainIdeas.description: long, slow climbs through the strings in the introduction.

mainIdeas.name: The rhythm
mainIdeas.description: a skipping long-short-long figure in six beats, on which the whole fast section is built.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a light, dancing tune, first on the flute, then shouted by the whole orchestra.

stops.hear: A loud chord, and an oboe holds a gentle line; then long scales climb slowly through the strings
Oboes and clarinets play a light, swaying tune in a new key
stops.happening: The introduction moves to C major

stops.hear: The same tune, now in another key
Flutes and violins toss a single note back and forth, hesitating
stops.happening: More than sixty repetitions of the note E: the bridge to the fast music

stops.hear: A flute plays a skipping tune in long-short-long rhythm
The whole orchestra takes up the tune, loud and exuberant
stops.happening: Theme 1 in full, in A major

stops.hear: The skipping flute tune starts again
Sudden quiet; the rhythm is passed around in fragments and through new keys
The theme bursts back in the full orchestra
The music drops to a whisper; under it, the basses grind a two-bar pattern over and over while the rest of the orchestra slowly builds
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], with an [[ostinato|ostinato]] over a long-held E

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The horns whoop the rhythm; a blazing close in A major

notice: Once the *Vivace* starts, tap the long-short-long rhythm. It is in almost every bar until the end.
In the coda, listen to the basses. The same two bars come round ten times, growing louder each time.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Kleiber recorded the Seventh in the Musikverein in November 1975 and January 1976. He takes the repeats in the first and last movements. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 5–8; tracks 1–4 are his Fifth, the recording used for our guide to that symphony.

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: A solemn procession in A minor, built on one walking rhythm: long, short-short, long, long. It starts very low and quiet, and each time it returns another layer is added on top. It was so popular at the first performance that it had to be played again at once.

mainIdeas.name: The rhythm
mainIdeas.description: long, short-short, long, long. The tune is almost all on one note; it is mostly rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The countermelody
mainIdeas.description: a sad, singing line that weaves around the rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The major-key melody
mainIdeas.description: a calm song for clarinets and bassoons in the middle.

stops.hear: A single soft chord in the woodwinds and horns, held and fading
stops.happening: An opening chord that sounds unfinished. The same chord will close the movement

stops.hear: Violas, cellos and basses, very quietly, play a plain tune in a walking rhythm
stops.happening: The theme, in A minor: an [[ostinato|ostinato]] rhythm, long, short-short, long, long

stops.hear: The second violins take the tune; under it, the violas and cellos add a sad, singing countermelody
stops.happening: The theme in layers, a little like a [[passacaglia|passacaglia]]

stops.hear: The first violins take the tune, with the others still singing below
The whole orchestra plays the theme at full strength
stops.happening: The climax of the first section

stops.hear: The key turns to A major; clarinets and bassoons sing a gentle melody over soft triplets in the violins
The walking rhythm returns in A minor
The strings enter one by one on the theme, quietly at first, then building
A brief return of the major-key melody

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The theme breaks into fragments passed between instruments; the opening chord returns

notice: The rhythm never stops. Listen to how it moves from the low strings to the violins to the whole orchestra, while new melodies pile up above it.
The first and last sounds are the same unresolved chord.

movements.heading: Presto – Assai meno presto
movements.summary: A [[scherzo|scherzo]] at top speed in F major, full of sudden loud bursts. Twice it gives way to a slow, glowing [[trio|trio]] in D major, a hymn-like tune said to be based on an Austrian pilgrims’ song, sung by the woodwinds while the violins hold one high note. The movement ends with a joke: the hymn starts a third time and is cut off.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo
mainIdeas.description: quick, scurrying music tossed between strings and woodwinds, with sudden loud outbursts.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a slow, swaying hymn in the woodwinds and horns over a long-held note in the violins.

stops.hear: A loud burst, then fast, light, scurrying music tossed between strings and woodwinds
Slower and hushed: clarinets, bassoons and horns sing a calm, hymn-like tune while the violins hold a single high note
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], in D major. The held note is a [[pedal-note|pedal note]]

stops.hear: The hymn swells to full strength; trumpets and drums ring out
The scurrying music returns
The hymn again
The scherzo a third time

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The hymn begins once more, is cut short, and five loud chords end the movement
stops.happening: Beethoven teases us with a third trio

notice: In the trio, listen to the violins’ held note. It hangs over the hymn for the whole section, like a drone.

movements.heading: Allegro con brio
movements.summary: Fast and furious from the first bar to the last. Two violent chords set off a whirling tune with a heavy kick on the second beat, and the energy never drops. Near the end the basses grind a two-note growl underneath while the orchestra rises to a dynamic Beethoven rarely asked for: *fff*, as loud as possible.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a whirling tune in the violins, with heavy accents off the main beat.

mainIdeas.name: The growl
mainIdeas.description: a two-note pattern in the basses that drives the coda.

stops.hear: Two violent chords; then a whirling, stamping tune in the violins, with a heavy accent on the second beat
A new tune in a dotted rhythm, at the same breathless speed
The two chords and the whirling tune again
The tune is pushed into new keys; the energy never drops
The opening blaze again
The basses churn a two-note growl over and over while the rest of the orchestra rises and rises

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The loudest music in the symphony
stops.happening: Beethoven marks it *fff*, a rare instruction in his music

notice: Listen for the accent on the second beat of the bar. It is what makes the finale stamp instead of run.

threads.title: Rhythm first
threads.body: Each movement is driven by one rhythm: the skipping long-short-long of the first, the walk of the second, the scurry of the third, the stamp of the finale.

threads.title: Long held notes
threads.body: The repeated E before the *Vivace*, the drone of the trio, the ground bass of both codas: under the dance there is always something that does not move.

threads.title: Three keys
threads.body: A major is home, but C major and F major keep breaking in: in the introduction, in the first movement’s development and in the scherzo, which is in F.
